Cluster A refrigeration loop: compressor suction pressure abnormally low. Technician leak check found refrigerant loss at a service valve. Air dampers respond normally.
Cluster B refrigeration loop pressures and compressor current are normal. Both supply-air dampers remain commanded open but physically stuck near closed. Actuator linkage is binding.
After sealing the service valve and restoring refrigerant in Cluster A, A1/A2 return below 4.5°C within 35 minutes. B1/B2 remain above 8.5°C.
Before Cluster A repair, technicians manually opened the Cluster B dampers. B1/B2 began cooling immediately while A1/A2 remained warm until their refrigeration-loop repair.
Facility power, outdoor temperature, central supervisory controller, and site network remained within normal ranges. No single site-wide failure is recorded.

causal_assessment.preferred_cause: Dual independent failures: A refrigerant leak in Cluster A and a mechanical damper binding in Cluster B.

action.recommended_action: Maintain manual damper overrides for Cluster B while completing the mechanical repair of the actuator linkage; continue monitoring Cluster A temperatures following the refrigerant recharge.
action.reason: Evidence E04 and E05 confirm that Cluster A and Cluster B are independent systems. Repairing Cluster A did not affect Cluster B, and manual intervention on Cluster B dampers successfully lowered temperatures. A single root cause is not supported by the evidence.

evidence.claim: Cluster A failure is caused by a refrigerant leak at a service valve.
Cluster B failure is caused by physically stuck supply-air dampers due to binding actuator linkage.
The incident is not a site-wide power or controller failure, supporting independent localized failures.

uncertainty: The specific cause of the actuator linkage binding in Cluster B (e.g., wear, debris, or mechanical fatigue) is not identified.
The specific cause of the refrigerant leak at the service valve in Cluster A (e.g., seal failure, vibration, or improper installation) is not identified.

next_test.test: Perform a mechanical inspection and lubrication/replacement of the Cluster B actuator linkage to ensure the dampers remain in the commanded position without manual intervention.
next_test.outcome_a_implication: If dampers remain open and temperatures stabilize, the mechanical binding is confirmed as the sole cause for Cluster B.
next_test.outcome_b_implication: If dampers remain stuck or temperatures rise, further investigation into the linkage mechanism or secondary airflow obstructions is required.
